question: Does QLoRA on the verified-pass corpus move HumanEval+ on the served quant by the ladder's +3pp admission threshold, and does the gain survive q4_K_M?
design: 2x2: {base, tuned} x {q4_K_M, f16}, greedy HumanEval+ pass@1, every arm through the same front door

protocol.eval: EvalPlus 0.3.1, --backend openai, --greedy, dataset humaneval (164 tasks, base + plus tests)
protocol.server: llama-server bundled with ollama (/usr/local/lib/ollama/llama-server, reports version 1 b4d6c7d8f), --jinja -c 4096 -ngl 99
protocol.note: f16 arms cannot run on rig_a (6 GB < 6.2 GB weights); host differs by precision, never within a comparison pair

backends.gpu: the primary set (gpu/): CUDA via GGML_BACKEND_PATH=/usr/local/lib/ollama/cuda_v13/libggml-cuda.so. Placement verified by VRAM check before each arm.
backends.cpu: an accidental first pass (cpu/), kept as a robustness cross-check: without GGML_BACKEND_PATH the ollama-bundled llama-server silently ignores -ngl and runs on CPU. Its base-f16 arm was stopped at task 8 when the fallback was noticed, so cpu/ has three arms only.
backends.why_it_matters: same artifacts, greedy decode: the tuned-q4 minus base-q4 HumanEval+ delta is +1.9pp on the GPU backend and -0.7pp on the CPU backend. Backend numerics alone move a greedy single-run delta by more than half the ladder's 3pp admission threshold.

base-f16.file: base-f16.gguf, convert_hf_to_gguf.py --outtype f16 over the training base checkpoint

tuned-f16.file: tuned-f16.gguf, same converter over the merged 16-bit checkpoint

tuned-q4.file: tuned-q4_K_M.gguf, llama-quantize q4_K_M over tuned-f16.gguf; sha verified identical on both rigs

training.recipe: tools/finetune/train_qlora.py at this record's commit: QLoRA r16 alpha16, ChatML, loss on assistant tokens only, 3 epochs, lr 2e-4 linear, seed 3407
training.dataset: tools/finetune/build_dataset.py --cap 40: 658 train / 80 val over 20 tasks, all TypeScript; manifest vendored beside this file
training.trainer_host: rig_b (RTX 3060 12 GB), 1919 s wall-clock, train_loss 0.196, final eval_loss 0.218
training.caveat: the corpus is 20 distinct problems in one language; see #197
